numerical_audit.cell_count_warning: 14s8p=112 cells; 12s10p=120 cells. This refutes an automatic cell-count saving at similar installed energy, not every possible usable-energy benefit.
numerical_audit.interpretation: 8% is the increase relative to original cost. It is 7.52 percentage points of revenue here; margin changes from 6% to -1.52%.
numerical_audit.model: Assume sale price P=100, original revenue-based margin m=0.06, cost C=94, battery share b=0.40 of C, pack price shock d=0.20; hold price and all other costs fixed.
numerical_audit.smaller_pack_warning: After a 10% reduction of the original battery cost, a subsequent 20% price shock gives C=97.008 and margin 2.992%, before added converter cost. The chat's shortcut omitted the upfront saving. This does not establish a viable hedge.
numerical_audit.warning: Illustrative premises only; no current price or investment recommendation.

stages.next_question: Which margin measure, pack specification, period and performance envelope are intended?
stages.rationale_summary: Preserve the user's business concern and performance constraint; classify DC/DC and chemistry changes as proposals. The 40% share comes from the assistant.
stages.title: 1 · Intake: outcome versus mechanism

stages.next_question: Is the concern voltage-limited performance, inaccessible usable energy, or procurement substitution?
stages.rationale_summary: The Y-inverter is introduced. The assistant initially strengthens the cheaper-pack argument, but examples do not prove vehicle-level economics.
stages.title: 2 · First technical branch

stages.next_question: How much usable energy is actually inaccessible under the required duty cycle?
stages.rationale_summary: Keep the earlier cell-saving claim and connect its counterargument. Separate series count, total energy, usable energy and current limits.
stages.title: 3 · Contradiction retained

stages.next_question: Do switching savings exceed NRE, qualification, inventory and service costs?
stages.rationale_summary: Add a distinct intervention: prequalified powertrain families. The assistant preference changes; this is not a human selection.
stages.title: 4 · Manufacturing alternative

stages.next_question: What else could explain the same quotation movement?
stages.rationale_summary: The explanation gravitates to architectural lock-in. FrameShift should retain that as a hypothesis and seek competing causes before declaring a root cause.
stages.title: 5 · Five Whys narrows too soon

stages.next_question: Do matched quotes support raw-material, supplier-power, capacity or landed-cost explanations?
stages.rationale_summary: The human challenges the assumed cause: single source or supply stress? Introduce alternatives and request evidence; do not record single source as a fact.
stages.title: 6 · Human expands the causal model

stages.next_question: Which observation would distinguish the competing mechanisms?
stages.rationale_summary: Add breadth and causal tests. Treat AND/OR examples and correlation numbers in the conversation as illustrations, not established gates or measured results.
stages.title: 7 · From a chain to a graph

stages.next_question: Are we designing the tool or solving the battery case in this session?
stages.rationale_summary: A second concern emerges: build an interactive reasoning system. Link the battery case as motivating evidence; keep its unresolved objective visible.
stages.title: 8 · A linked product concern

stages.next_question: Who can authorize the business boundary and own success measures?
stages.rationale_summary: Separate the why/how ladder from cause/effect. Business framing opens procurement and commercial options; wider scope still needs an accountable owner.
stages.title: 9 · Explicit reframing

stages.next_question: What was actually created and validated, versus merely proposed in the conversation?
stages.rationale_summary: The source navigator records naming and a public-repository request. The detailed assistant turns 10–11 were not inspected; no repository execution is inferred from them.
stages.title: 10 · Naming and repository branch

stages.next_question: What evidence and human-owned criteria would justify selecting an architecture?
stages.rationale_summary: The slide narrative returns to margin. It offers an architecture preference without OEM evidence, approved criteria or a signed decision. A document request is not validation.
stages.title: 11 · Return to the original outcome

stages.next_question: Which candidate frame should a human approve for a real runtime session?
stages.rationale_summary: Proposed next sequence: correct intake; approve one frame; gather evidence; accept an option set including baseline; confirm criteria; compare scenarios; ask for a decision.
stages.title: 12 · FrameShift handoff

test_findings: Preserve counterarguments instead of overwriting prior claims.
Human suggestions of single source and capacity stress are not measured OEM facts.
The assistant repeatedly changes its preferred topology; no approved decision follows.
A broader frame is a candidate and needs an owner; it is not automatically superior.
The historical JSON example mixes epistemic type and lifecycle status; use current schema types and ordinal confidence.
Do not infer causal AND/OR gates or confidence probabilities from illustrative prose.
Factory sourcing timescales and runtime SOC variation need separate requirements.
The complete map is a typed directed graph, not a tree: evidence, contradictions and shared interventions create cross-links.
